original_question: How should alternating virtual knots be defined and classified, what is the correct analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture in the virtual setting, and how can one classify alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization?
correct_elements: The draft already captures all three components of the paper's official problem almost verbatim: (i) define and classify alternating virtual knots, (ii) find the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture, and (iii) classify alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization. It also correctly keeps the scope narrow and topological rather than drifting into unrelated invariants.
missing_details: The paper's ambient model of a virtual knot should be stated: virtual knot theory is interpreted as embeddings of curves in thickened surfaces, taken up to addition and removal of empty handles; equivalently, virtual diagrams correspond to stable equivalence classes of links in thickened surfaces.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say that the sought definition of "alternating" is to be formulated inside that virtual/surface model, rather than assumed from the classical planar case.
The paper's wording asks not only to identify an analogue of Tait's flyping conjecture, but to find it and prove it.

The phrase "without stabilization" needs unpacking: in the paper's surface model, stabilization means addition or subtraction of empty handles, so this clause asks for classification on fixed surfaces before passing to stable equivalence.
The paper explicitly says "Compare [110]"; that comparison cue is missing from the draft.

The nearest official formulation is an open problem about alternating virtual knots and alternating weaves on surfaces; the draft should avoid broadening this into a general classification problem for all virtual links or tangles.
No ambient ring/field, variables, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers occur here; this is a topological classification problem, so those algebraic data are not applicable.
refined_question: Using the interpretation of virtual knots as stable equivalence classes of embeddings in thickened surfaces, determine an appropriate definition of an alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots in that sense, formulate and prove the correct virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture, and, prior to passing to stable equivalence, classify alternating weaves on fixed surfaces (that is, without allowing stabilization or destabilization by adding or removing empty handles).
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's official open problem in Section 3, item 15, whose text is: "Define and classify alternating virtual knots. Find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it. Compare [110] Classify all alternating weaves on surfaces (without stabilization)." The missing context needed to make this stand-alone comes from Section 2 and especially Section 2.2, where virtual knots are interpreted as stable classes of links embedded in thickened surfaces and stable equivalence is defined via isotopy, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition/subtraction of empty handles. From that context, the phrase "without stabilization" is naturally read as classification on fixed surfaces before quotienting by handle addition/removal. I do not give an alternate formulation because this paper states the problem directly and does not, nearby, prove an explicit equivalent reformulation of it.

[110] P. Zinn-Justin and J. B. Zuber, cited by Problem 15 via "Compare [110]"
